payload.headline: Alphabet falls 2.7% to 265.29, below the buy zone; next buy at 234.35

summary.thesis: Sales are growing faster and margins are rising, but free cash flow fell from 73.6B to 19.7B and profit forecasts keep dropping, so the price is hard to justify on cash today.
summary.decision: Hold the small first position from yesterday and stop buying, because the close of 265.29 broke below 271.77, the line set in yesterday's plan.
summary.act_at: Add at 234.35; no new buying above it

payload.happening: Alphabet closed at 265.29, down 2.7% on the day. It fell through the 271.77–277.07 zone that was the buy zone yesterday, and that zone now sits above the price as resistance (a ceiling where selling showed up before). CNBC reported a wider AI-stock sell-off that wiped out the Nasdaq's 2026 gains, and The Verge reported that YouTube is preparing to settle social media addiction claims for $3 billion, which no filing has confirmed. There is no earnings date in the data.
payload.business: The business itself is still growing. Quarterly revenue grew 24.65% from a year earlier, faster than the 21.79% two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from the core business per dollar of sales) rose to 33.32% from 32.19%. The weak spot is cash. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and paying for new investment) was 19.7B over the last 12 months, against 73.6B a year earlier, so the free-cash-flow margin is only 4.19%. The filings flag that heavy spending is not paying back yet: each dollar invested now earns 24¢ a year, against 40¢ three years ago. They also flag that reported profit leans on one-off gains, which is why the 50.03% net margin is higher than the 33.32% operating margin. Analysts have cut this year's EPS (earnings per share) estimate by 5.2% over 30 days, to 19.56. Today's news mostly moves sentiment and legal exposure, not demand. The market-wide AI sell-off is sentiment. The reported $3 billion YouTube settlement is a legal and governance cost, and it is small next to 139.0B of net cash (cash and investments minus debt). Turning off Google Assistant on smart speakers is a minor product decision. What is at risk is how fast the heavy spending turns back into cash. Revenue growth and the balance sheet are not at risk.

worth.text: The valuation methods disagree a lot. On earnings the stock looks cheap: 13.9 times trailing earnings and 13.6 times this year's estimate. But it is 17.7 times next year's estimate, because analysts expect EPS to fall to 14.97. Measured on cash, it looks very expensive. A discounted cash flow model (which values the company today based on the cash it is expected to produce in the future) starts from the 19.7B of free cash flow and gives 25.95 to 70.13 per share, with 51.37 in the middle. Even at 30% starting growth, that model only reaches 78.06. Against its own past, the stock is about fair. Its price-to-sales ratio (market value divided by yearly revenue) is at the 46th percentile of its last 5 years, which gives a range of 234.35 to 375.22 with 279.84 in the middle. Against its peers it is expensive: 7.0 times sales, against a peer median of 4.8. Almost the whole gap between the methods comes from the cash starting point. The cash-flow model takes the depressed 19.7B as normal. The own-history range assumes Alphabet will produce cash the way it used to. My range is 234.35 to 279.84, so today's 265.29 sits in the lower half of a range that only holds if cash flow recovers.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers from 19.7B toward the earlier 73.6B as the current spending cycle pays off; if it stays near 19.7B, even 234.35 is generous.

bull: Revenue growth is speeding up: the latest quarter grew 24.65% from a year earlier, against 21.79% two quarters ago.
Margins are rising while the company spends heavily: operating margin is 33.32%, up from 32.19%.
The balance sheet is strong, with 139.0B of net cash, and price-to-sales sits at only the 46th percentile of its own 5-year range.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 19.7B over the last 12 months from 73.6B, and the cash-flow model's middle value is 51.37 per share.
Forecasts are falling: this year's EPS estimate was cut 5.2% in 30 days to 19.56, and next year's estimate is 14.97.
It is pricier than its peers, at 7.0 times sales against a peer median of 4.8, and the filings say the price needs about 37% a year growth against 17% a year delivered over 3 years.

levels.what: Today's close, below 271.77. Under yesterday's plan, a close below that line means no new buying here. Keep the small first position.
Low end of the own-history range and the add level. It leaves room for error if free cash flow stays near 19.7B.
Middle of the own-history range. Above it the stock is no longer cheap against its own past, so there is no adding above this price.

longterm.why: The business is growing, but cash flow has not recovered and estimates are still falling. The price also broke the line that yesterday's plan set, so the plan says hold and add only at 234.35.

swing.why: The price is below its 20-day (289.45), 50-day (322.3) and 200-day (336.71) averages, and the data shows no support level below it. No trade until a daily close back above 277.07, with a first target of 293.72.

decision.timing: With no earnings date in the data, price levels and estimate changes set the timing: the December options imply a move of about 8.4% by 2026-12-18, and the put/call open-interest ratio of 1.37 (more open bets on a fall than on a rise) points to more pressure before a base forms.

change_mind: A daily close back above 277.07 while this year's EPS estimate stops falling from 19.56 would put buying back on the table above 234.35.
The next filing showing trailing free cash flow clearly rising from 19.7B toward 73.6B would raise the fair-value range toward 279.84 and above.

A filing confirming legal costs well beyond the reported $3 billion YouTube settlement, or another cut to this year's EPS estimate beyond the 5.2% in 30 days, would move the decision from hold to trim above 279.84.
payload.what_changed: Changed: the long-term call moved from buy to hold, because the 265.29 close fell below 271.77, which yesterday's plan set as the line for no more buying above 234.35.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
